transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. It's probably nothing major, but my wife actually suggested I make an appointment. 

What really brought me in is... well, she'll be telling me about things, like my cousin’s upcoming appointments or who is giving him rides, and I’m looking right at her, nodding along... but a minute later I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she said. I feel awful about it, because I really am trying to be a good listener for her. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm in the right place and answering your question okay.
Does this happen only when your wife is talking to you, or do you find yourself having trouble following conversations with other people as well?

Oh, um, that's a really good question. I haven't really... I don't think I've noticed it as much with other people. 

But, well, since I'm not working right now, I'm mostly just at home with my wife, so she's the one I talk to the most. When I do chat with the neighbors or, you know, folks at the hardware store, I think I do okay? I really try my best to be polite and give people my full attention. I definitely don't want to make it sound like I'm just ignoring everyone around me, because I'm really not. It just seems to be those longer conversations at home where I sort of... drift. 

I hope that answers your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you feel more anxious or stressed when talking to your wife compared to when you're talking to other people?

Oh, no, no. Not at all. I really don't feel stressed or anxious with her. We have a wonderful marriage, honestly. She's been so supportive, especially since I haven't been working. I definitely don't want to give you the impression that she stresses me out or that we don't get along, because that's not it at all. 

It's just... well, I just feel terrible when I realize I've kind of drifted off, because I want to be a good husband and give her my full attention. I hope it didn't sound like I was complaining about her earlier? She really is very patient with me. I just want to make sure I'm explaining things right so I'm actually being helpful to you. Does that make sense?
Do you often find yourself forgetting things that happened earlier in the day or things your wife told you about?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I forget a lot of things, really. Just little things here and there, you know? Like, lately, I've had a few moments where I meant to do something and it just slipped my mind. 

Like, um, returning a call from the doctor's office, or picking up a prescription. And there was one time I didn't leave the house quite on time for one of my cousin's appointments. But I really try my best to stay on top of things! I don't want you to think I'm completely disorganized or dropping the ball on everything, because I'm usually pretty good about trying to keep track. It's just a few little slip-ups recently. 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
Do you have trouble focusing on tasks or activities outside of conversations with your wife?

Oh, um... well, maybe a little bit? I don't want to make it sound like I can't get anything done, because I really do try to stay focused. I want to be useful, you know? 

But sometimes... well, if I sit down to help out with something, like working out a catering order or listening in on a planning call for the parish... I always start off just fine. I'm right there, paying attention. But then, before too long, my mind just sort of... wanders off a bit. And then I realize I have to go back over the same notes because it's like I never even read them the first time. 

It's just a little frustrating, but I really am trying my best to stay on task. I hope that doesn't make me sound too scatterbrained? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way. Is that what you were looking for?
Do you ever feel like you're in a fog or a daze, where things seem unclear or distant?

Oh, a fog? Um... no, I don't think so. I wouldn't say I ever feel like I'm in a daze or anything like that. I mean, I'm fully awake and aware of where I am and what's going on around me. I definitely don't want to give you the impression that I'm, you know, completely spaced out or disconnected from reality. 

It's really just that my attention slips away sometimes, like I mentioned before. But my head feels clear! I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong idea about how I'm functioning. Am I explaining that okay?
Do you often feel mentally tired or exhausted after trying to focus or pay attention?

Oh, mentally exhausted? Um... no, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, maybe just your normal, everyday tiredness by the time the evening rolls around, but certainly not from trying to pay attention. 

I actually feel like I have a pretty good amount of energy! I definitely don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling drained or lazy all day. When my mind wanders off, like I was saying before, it's not because my brain is too tired to keep going... the thought just sort of slips away for a second. I can usually jump right back in without needing to rest or take a break or anything like that. 

Is that a good sign? I really hope that's the kind of information you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful!
Has there been any significant change or stress in your life recently, aside from not working?

Oh, stress? Um... well, I wouldn't say it's been *too* stressful, really. We're very blessed, honestly. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or that things are bad at home, because they really aren't! 

But... well, I guess things have been just a little bit busier for about the last 11 months or so. My cousin had to have surgery, and so he moved in with us while he recovers. It's been wonderful having family around, it really has! I love being able to help him out. It's just... maybe since then, with the extra activity in the house, that's when I noticed it getting a little harder to keep my thoughts straight. 

It's not his fault at all, of course! I just want to be sure I'm giving you the full picture. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about.
Do you have trouble learning new things, like a new skill or a new hobby?

Oh, learning new things? Um... no, I wouldn't say I have trouble with that. I mean, I'm not taking any college classes right now or anything, but I definitely still enjoy picking up a new book or trying a new recipe. 

I really don't want you to think my brain is slowing down or that I can't catch on to things! If someone shows me how to do something, I can usually get the hang of it just fine. Maybe I have to read the instructions a couple of times, but that's just being thorough, right? I'm sure everybody does that. 

I just try my best to keep my mind active. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job explaining things for you.
Did your trouble with focusing and following conversations start around the same time your cousin moved in with you?

Oh, did it start when he moved in? Um... well... I guess I'd have to say no, not exactly. I mean, the extra activity in the house definitely made it a little more noticeable lately, but... 

I don't want to make it sound like I've always had something wrong with me, because I really haven't! I've always tried so hard to do my best. But if I'm being completely honest, it goes back a lot further than that. Even way back in grade school, definitely before I was 12, my teachers used to tell my parents that I was a very bright boy. Which was always so nice of them to say! But... well, they also said I was always daydreaming. I guess I'd accidentally leave my homework inside my desk a lot, and they'd have to give me little reminders to finish up my classwork. 

I'm sure it was just normal kid stuff, right? Just having your head in the clouds a bit. I definitely wasn't a bad student or a troublemaker, I promise! I hope it's okay that I'm bringing up things from that long ago. Is that the kind of background information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you experienced difficulties with focusing or paying attention consistently throughout your life?

Oh, consistently throughout my life? Um... well, I wouldn't say it's been a constant, terrible struggle or anything like that. I've managed just fine, really! I've had jobs and, you know, raised a family, so I don't want to make it sound like I couldn't function. 

But... I suppose if I look back, maybe there have been times here and there where I had to work a little harder than other people to keep my mind on track. Just little things, like having to reread a paragraph or needing to make extra lists to keep myself organized. It hasn't been a big, dramatic problem, I promise! Just... maybe a mild, sort of background thing that I just learned to work around over the years. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm trying not to exaggerate, but I also want to be honest with you. Am I explaining that alright?
Do you think your mind wandering happens more often in quiet, one-on-one conversations or in louder, more chaotic environments?

Oh, quiet versus loud environments? Um... gosh, I'm actually not entirely sure about that. I haven't really noticed a specific pattern, to be perfectly honest. 

I mean, if there's a lot of commotion going on, I suppose anyone might get a little bit distracted, right? But I wouldn't say my mind wanders terribly in either situation. I always try my absolute best to give whoever is talking my full attention, whether it's just the two of us or if we're in a busy room. I'd hate for anyone to think I was being rude or ignoring them! It's really just a brief little drift here and there, nothing major. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a very clear answer for that one? I'm trying to be as helpful as I can, I just haven't really kept track of which situation makes it happen more. Is that okay? I can try to think on it harder if you need me to!
Did you have any symptoms of hyperactivity, such as fidgeting or restlessness, when you were a child?

Oh, hyperactivity? Like... bouncing around and not sitting still? Um, no, I really don't think so. I was actually a very quiet little boy. I always tried my absolute best to be polite and not cause any trouble for my parents or the teachers. 

I mean, maybe I'd tap my pencil every now and then, just like any normal kid might, but I definitely wasn't restless or disruptive! I always wanted to be a good student and do exactly what I was told. So... no, I wouldn't say I had anything like that going on. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know. Is that helpful?
Have you ever been diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder or had concerns raised about it by a doctor or teacher?

Oh, diagnosed with it? Um, no. No, I've never had any sort of diagnosis like that. 

I mean, I think if a teacher or a doctor had ever been worried about me, they would have said something, right? But I always tried so hard to be a good student, so they never really had any reason to bring anything up. I got decent grades and, you know, I was polite, so I don't think anyone ever thought there was a problem. 

I've just always tried to do my best and not be a burden to anyone. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I was hiding some big diagnosis from you. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed your mind wandering or having trouble focusing in situations other than conversations with your wife?

Oh, other situations? Um... well, I suppose there are a couple of little things. I do try to keep busy and help out where I can. Like, if I sit down to work out a catering order, or if I'm listening through a parish planning call... I always start off perfectly fine, really trying to do a good job and pay close attention. 

But I guess, before too long, my mind might wander just a tiny bit. I'll suddenly realize I have to go back over the exact same notes, almost like I never read them in the first place. 

It's really nothing major, though! I always make sure to double-check everything so I don't mess up the orders or let anyone at the parish down. I'd hate to be a bother or make mistakes that cause extra work for anyone else. Is that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Do you often avoid tasks that require sustained mental effort?

Oh, avoid them? Um... no, no, I really don't think I do that. I always try my absolute best to just tackle whatever needs doing, even if it takes a lot of thinking or... or extra time. 

I wouldn't ever want to leave the hard work for my wife or the folks at the parish, you know? That wouldn't be very fair of me at all. So I just make sure to sit down and get it done, because I really want to pull my weight and be helpful. I would feel terrible if someone else had to pick up my slack just because something was a little difficult. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just try very hard not to shy away from my responsibilities. Does that answer your question alright?
Have you ever acted on impulse without thinking through the consequences?

Acted on impulse? Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. I'm actually a very careful person, I think. 

I always try to think things all the way through before I make a decision or do anything. I would just feel absolutely awful if I did something rash and it ended up causing a problem for my wife, or if it made extra work for the folks at the parish. I always try to be very considerate of how my actions might affect other people, you know? 

So I really try to look before I leap, as they say. I hope that's a good thing? I just wouldn't want you to think I was out there being reckless or causing trouble for anyone. Am I making sense?
Did you experience difficulties with focusing or paying attention as a child, similar to what you're experiencing now?

Oh, as a child? Um... well, I suppose so, yes. My parents used to tell me that back in grade school—definitely before I was 12 or so—my teachers would always say I was a very bright boy, which was really nice of them to say! But... um, they did mention I was maybe a little bit of a daydreamer. 

I guess I would sometimes accidentally leave my homework inside my desk, or they would have to give me a gentle little reminder to finish up my classwork. It wasn't that I was trying to be difficult or disobedient, I promise! I always wanted to be a good student and make my teachers happy. I just... sort of got lost in my own thoughts sometimes, I suppose. 

It wasn't anything too terrible, just little mistakes here and there. I hope that makes sense? Is that the kind of childhood example you were looking for?
Did you often struggle with organization and time management as a child?

Organization and time management when I was little? Um... no, I don't believe so. I really don't remember having any trouble with that sort of thing. 

My mother was always very good about keeping everything tidy and on schedule, so I just tried my best to follow her lead. I wouldn't have wanted to cause any fuss or make her late for anything, you know? I always tried to keep my room neat and be ready when it was time to go to church or school. 

I'm sure I wasn't perfect, but I really did try to be a good boy and keep my things where they belonged. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was a messy child or caused trouble for my parents. Does that sound alright? I hope that's helpful.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety as an adult?

Restless or fidgety? Oh, um... no, not really. I don't think I'm a fidgety person at all. 

I'm actually quite happy just sitting quietly, maybe reading a nice book or listening to the radio. I wouldn't want to be one of those people who's always pacing around or tapping their feet and making other people nervous, you know? I always try to be very calm and respectful of the space around me, especially when my wife is trying to relax in the evenings. 

I mean, I suppose everyone gets a little stiff if they sit in one place for too long, but I certainly don't feel... agitated or anything like that. I hope that's the right answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I was a nervous or disruptive sort of person.
